💬 Baghdad hosts 52nd OIC foreign ministers’ meeting with Iran FM in attendance

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The 52nd session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) opened in Baghdad on Saturday, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in attendance.

According to the Iraqi News Agency, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi inaugurated the meeting, which brings together representatives of all OIC member states.
​
Ambassador Hassanein Kamil, spokesperson for the meeting, said Baghdad took over the council’s presidency from Turkiye following the opening ceremony.
​
He added that representatives of all OIC member states were attending the gathering, alongside a representative of the United Nations secretary-general. Forty international organizations are also participating in the meeting, Kamil said.
​
Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Baghdad on Saturday morning to attend the two-day session, scheduled for October 17-18. He was welcomed at the airport by an Iraqi deputy foreign minister.
​
During his visit, Araghchi is scheduled to address the meeting and hold bilateral talks with his counterparts from Islamic countries.
​
The meeting is being held under the central theme of “Dialogue and Solidarity: Two Fundamental Pillars for Promoting Peace and Sustainable Development,” underscoring the gathering’s focus on cooperation among OIC member states.
​
The OIC brings together Muslim-majority countries and other member states to coordinate positions on issues of common concern, including regional developments and cooperation among Islamic nations.

🇺🇦🇲🇩 Ukrainian border guards chase a draft dodger across the river into Moldova, beat him with an oar, end up detained by Moldovan police

A video circulating on Moldovan social media shows a Ukrainian man swimming across the river from Ukraine to Moldova while border guards in a motorboat try to stop him, hitting him with an oar. He made it across.

The guards' boat then drifted onto the Moldovan bank, where local residents blocked it and called the police. Furious Moldovans cursed out the guards and accused them of drowning people in the river.

"You came into my country, you're drowning people," one local told them.

According to Moldova's Border Police, the incident took place on October 15 around 3pm near the village of Holoshnitsa. A patrol detained the two Ukrainian border guards and took them to the Border Police station in Kosautsy.

Moldovan prosecutors have opened a criminal case for illegal crossing of the state border under Article 362 of Moldova's Criminal Code.

Ukraine's State Border Guard Service called it an "incident" during the detention of a border violator and says an internal investigation is underway.

❔🇺🇦 Ukrainian media "Strana" on what's happening with Starlink for the Ukrainian Armed Forces:

On Wednesday morning, October 14th, Ukraine announced that Starlink had limited the speed of its Starshield system for the needs of the Ukrainian Armed Forces to 160 km/h.

However, on Thursday, several Ukrainian and Western media outlets, citing sources in the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense, reported that the Starshield service had resumed its operation.

However, this was not officially confirmed by anyone.

The situation became clearer yesterday.

A Reuters source in the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense reported that the receivers are now working while in motion, but only at a speed of up to 160 km/h. That is, slower than before. As a reminder, Ukrainian volunteers and experts had previously reported that the initial speed limit was set to this value. Subsequently, according to their information, the restrictions became even stricter, but now, according to Reuters, the speed has been increased again to 160 km/h, but not to the previous levels.

Yesterday, Zelensky also effectively confirmed this information. He said that the speed at which SpaceX provides internet access is being restored, but not fully yet.

As Ukrainian volunteers and journalists have stated, the 160 km/h limit has already disrupted a number of operations by the Ukrainian Armed Forces, especially in the area of "mid-range strikes" (i.e., attacks on Russian rear areas in territories occupied in Ukraine). It also limits the speed of operation of Ukrainian interceptor drones.

It is also now almost certain that this is not a technical malfunction (given that the service has not yet been fully restored), but a political decision by Washington. Apparently, this is a measure of pressure on Kiev due to Zelensky's refusal to stop attacks on oil refineries.

At the same time, it is also clear that this decision could not have been made without the consent of Trump.

📡 Pezeshkian: Short film captures current generation’s vision of world and future

📌 Tehran, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian has described short films as the voice of today’s generation and an opportunity for the creative narration of the realities of Iran and the world.

Iran is home to a people who, across the ages and sustained by their authentic culture and brilliant civilization, have consistently contributed to science and art, turning the efforts and creativity of successive generations into an enduring legacy for posterity, said Pezeshkian in a message to the 43rd Tehran International Short Film Festival, which will be held from October 17 to 22, 2026.
​
Today, this path continues in the thinking of the new generation, the message added.
​
Cinema is one of the most important languages for narrating this life and this culture, a language that can portray what people see, experience, and desire for their future, and share it with others, Pezeshkian stated.
​
By offering room for fresh perspectives, new experiences, and creative storytelling, short film conveys, truthfully and artistically, a portion of the reality of contemporary Iran and the world, he noted.
​
The Tehran International Short Film Festival serves as a valuable platform for these perspectives to converge and for dialogue between Iranian and international filmmakers, laying the groundwork for nations to better understand one another and for people to draw closer through art and culture, he stressed.
​
Now more than ever, we require art and narratives that draw people closer, open the way for dialogue and mutual understanding, and search for hope, empathy, and the prospect of building a better future within the everyday fabric of people’s lives, Pezeshkian wrote.

📲 @Irna_en​
